slides.title: Misinformation and Deepfakes
slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on Misinformation and Deepfakes.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn,
• Identify how **AI** generates fake content,
• Understand the dangers of **deepfake** media,
• Recognize the societal impact of misinformation, and
• Apply strategies for source verification.

slides.title: System Requirements
slides.narration:
A device with internet access.
A web browser to view examples.

slides.title: Prerequisites
slides.narration:
Basic understanding of how the internet works.
Familiarity with common online media.

slides.title: What are Deepfakes?
slides.narration:
Can you always trust what you see online?
**AI** can now create very real-looking fakes.
These fakes are called **Deepfakes**.
They can be audio, video, or images.
slides.image_prompt: AI creating fake content, digital art

slides.title: How AI Creates Fakes
slides.narration:
**Deep Learning** models learn patterns.
They study real faces, voices, and actions.
Then, they generate new, fake content.
It looks very convincing to us.
slides.image_prompt: Neural network generating faces, digital illustration

slides.title: Risks: Audio and Video
slides.narration:
Imagine a fake speech from a leader.
Or a fake call from a family member.
These can cause great confusion.
They can even spread false news.

slides.title: Risks: Images
slides.narration:
Fake images can defame people.
They can show events that never happened.
This changes public perception easily.
It affects trust in visual proof.

slides.title: Impact on Individuals
slides.narration:
A person's reputation can be ruined.
Their privacy can be deeply invaded.
This leads to emotional distress.
It can harm their personal life.
slides.image_prompt: Person looking distressed at a phone screen

slides.title: Impact on Society
slides.narration:
**Deepfakes** can sway elections.
They can create political instability.
Trust in news and media drops.
This challenges our shared reality.
slides.image_prompt: People arguing over news, societal division

slides.title: Verify Your Sources
slides.narration:
What is the origin of this content?
Does it come from a trusted news outlet?
Always check multiple reliable sources.
Cross-reference information you find.
slides.image_prompt: Magnifying glass over a newspaper, fact-checking

slides.title: Build Media Literacy
slides.narration:
Learn to spot signs of manipulation.
Look for unnatural movements or voices.
Question all sensational content.
Developing this skill is very important.
slides.image_prompt: Person reading news critically, media literacy

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
We covered **Deepfakes** and their risks.
We saw how **AI** creates fake content.
We discussed societal and personal impacts.
Remember to verify sources and build media literacy.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
Think of a recent news story.
Try to find its original source.
Check if other trusted sources report it.
This practice builds your critical skills.
